items.note: The page builds the tensor identity RF_s = 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A, states the chirp identity with a link for absorbing Q (its home page is chirp.md), and derives the cancellation of R. This matches the paper's route through Lemmas tensor-resampling and chirp-permutation.

per-line error less than p^2 of the one-dimensional algorithms, on which 'error below dp^2' rests

items.note: The identity is derived by tensoring, and the setup bound is derived. The rest is asserted: 'Both A and B_0 are contractions', 'Errors and times add over the d passes: error below dp^2', and the exposure cost (cited). The per-axis contraction and error p^2 that the d-pass sum needs are never shown.

This follows the paper: 'Since t_i >= r/2, each tensor map invokes at most sum_i T/t_i <= 2dT/r lines', then O(dTp^nu/r), and dividing by Tp gives O(dp^{nu-1}/r) -> 0 under the growth assumptions.

dropped: complex conjugation of the input and output of an algorithm for RF_s gives an algorithm for RF_s^+ with the same error bound (conjugation commutes with the real permutation R and preserves the disk grid and the norm). This is what lets the opposite transform run without executing R.
items.note: The identity is derived step by step, as in the paper. The page never says how RF_s^+ is computed, and the claim that no permutation is executed in the opposite transform needs that.
The page writes '(F_q^+R_beta z)_j = (1/q) sum_w z_{beta w} e^{2pi i wj/q}' and substitutes w' = beta w to get (R_beta^{-1}F_q^+ z)_j. This is correct and is the paper's substitution h = ck.
'Each t_i is a unit modulo s_i, and R applies R_{t_i} on axis i, so tensoring gives RF_s^+R = F_s^+'. Correct, because (P_{s_i}u)_j = u_{t_i j}, and t_i is a power of two while s_i is an odd prime.
F_s^+F_s = I/S is derived early from orthogonality of the exponentials and tensoring. The normalized convolution rule F_s(u*v) = S F_s u . F_s v is asserted, just as the paper asserts it.
Using that a permutation commutes with pointwise products, the left side becomes F_s^+(F_s u . F_s v) = (1/S)F_s^+F_s(u*v) = u*v/S^2, exactly as in the paper.

errors.quote: That page gives linear contractions $A$, $B_0$ ... with $P_sF_s=2^{2\alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA$, computed in time $O(tp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$ without executing $P_s$ or $P_t$.
errors.problem: The restated one-dimensional result leaves out the paper's error bound: the approximations have error less than p^2. The page later claims 'error below dp^2' for the tensor maps, which rests on that per-axis p^2 bound. The page also leaves the hypothesis theta = t/s - 1 > p/alpha^4 implicit ('with p, alpha, delta as there'), although its own setup only requires t_i > s_i.
